title: Downtown Canal Street memories and Tom Anderson's
summary: Mac remembers Canal Street shops, shining shoes, Tom Anderson's and the waiter Boleg.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Oh, I remember pretty good. I shined shoes, I was all in the house. So you take where Cotton's jewelry store, that used to be a barber shop on that corner. Right on the canal. And you take where the Lois State, that used to be a shooting gallery. And where the Sanger is now, that was something like a mummy. You used to go in there and look at all kinds of rubber and wax mummies. And where the F.W. Woolwork, that was a candy store. And coming down toward the Iberville, that was a hardware store. And in between where the parking lot is, right from the lady's club, that was a Tom Anderson's.

Tom Anderson's, yeah, he went out of there. The boardroom, huh? Yeah, Tom Anderson's, remember that Boleg used to throw a tray? Yeah, yeah. He kept three trays. Uh-huh. One on top of his head and one in each hand. It was delivered to the Spurgeon, remember, in the, in the, around there where the, that project is? That's where the, in the district, huh?

And he, you know, all the stuff he called out of him, and Boleg used to take three trays. He put one on his head and one in each hand. He kept, and he'd leave them to the door. The first one he'd leave them with it on his hand, see, and then he'd take the other one. He'd still carry that, and when he'd come back and pick up the dishes, he'd put them all on one tray and have them all on one in the head, you know. Never seen the last two times.
